text:
maya: Heads up — after the 2026-03 canary there’s a latency tail on small-seq FP8 workloads. p99 went from ~98ms to ~180ms on A100 SM86 when KV cache is warm.
liam: ugh, saw something similar in staging earlier today. did we change any triton/cutlass toggles in the build?
maya: Not intentionally. Build flag in the canary was "-DUSE_SM86_PREFETCH=OFF" to stabilize another regression. I tried flipping it locally and it changes behavior.
cheng: sharing quick repro steps i used:
```bash
./bench --model llama-13b --quant fp8 --seq 64 --batcher small_seq --kv-prefetch off --runs 100
# capture p50/p95/p99
```
maya: results from canary vs rollback:
```
canary (prefetch OFF): p99=182ms, p95=76ms, p50=22ms
rollback (prefetch ON): p99=104ms, p95=60ms, p50=21ms
```
sylvia: interesting — the p95 shift isn't huge but p99 doubles. smells like KV-cache eviction / pipeline stall for a subset of requests. Any flamegraph?
maya: attached a tiny flame snippet (pasted):
```
-- cpu: scheduling wait (small)
-- kernel: cutlass_fp8_v2 (fast path)
-- kernel: triton_dispatch_wait
-- kernel: fp8_dequantize_slowpath (rare but expensive)
```
liam: That slowpath dequantize jump looks like calibration mismatch -> runtime falling back. Could calibration of per-channel scales be picking outliers causing slow scalar path for some heads?
sylvia: +1. We saw a similar pattern when temporary calibration thresholds were widened. If dequant falls back to a reference routine it's very costly.
cheng: i profiled with nvprof and saw these kernels: `cutlass_fp8_matmul_fast`, `cutlass_fp8_matmul_fallback`, and `kv_prefetch_worker`. The fallback spikes correlate with requests that have short prompts (small_seq) and cold KV access followed by immediate hits.
perf-bot: perf-alert: canary-2026-03-15: fp8_p99_regression_detected (delta +84ms) — link: https://perf.redwood/run/2339
infra-bot: canary deployment 2026-03-15T09:32 rolled out to us-west-2-canary-pool (id: canary-2339).
maya: hypothesis: disabling prefetch increased concurrency on the KV worker, causing intermittent cache thrash; combined with calibration edgecases triggers fallback into scalar dequant path.
ops: can we test two toggles separately: 1) re-enable prefetch and 2) force CUTLASS kernel selection to alternate path to see which reduces p99?
liam: quick command to force kernel toggle locally:
```
export CUTLASS_KERNEL_MODE=alternate
./bench --model llama-13b --quant fp8 --seq 64 --batcher small_seq --kv-prefetch off
```
sylvia: also try forcing quant fallback to INT8 to compare quality vs perf: `--quant int8` — if int8 p99 is fine then fp8 path is the culprit.
cheng: ran matrix: (prefetch ON/OFF) x (kernel default/alternate) x (quant fp8/int8) over 500 runs. summary: 
- prefetch ON + kernel default + fp8: p99=110ms
- prefetch OFF + kernel default + fp8: p99=178ms
- prefetch OFF + kernel alternate + fp8: p99=118ms
- prefetch OFF + kernel default + int8: p99=107ms
so toggling kernel to alternate buys us most of the regression even when prefetch is off.
maya: great data. suggests kernel selector is choosing a slow fallback for some SM86 codegen variant when prefetch disabled. maybe the selector uses perf hints that assumed prefetch availability.
liam: action items:
1) cheng to add a probe in the selector to log chosen kernel + reason for each request (sample rate 1%) — need traces for canary.
2) ops to rollback the prefetch OFF flag in canary for now.
3) sylvia to check calibration histogram for recent model loads — any widened scale ranges?
4) maya to run nsight on canary replica hitting p99 requests.
cheng: i'll open a short-lived feature-branch to add selector debug logs and a guard that avoids choosing fallback when `kv_prefetch==off` unless fallback is strictly faster.
ops: rollback scheduled for 2026-03-15T10:05 (confirmed) :white_check_mark:
sylvia: calibration check: found a handful of heads with extreme outliers in the last 24h loads, we re-run calibration with clipping at 99.9 percentile and will push new profiles to canary.
maya: thanks. if selector-debug + re-calib + rollback all show improvements we can do a controlled rollout with kernel toggle disabled for canary until we have selector fix.
liam: one more note — build flags matter. the `-DUSE_SM86_PREFETCH` macro changes codepaths in the CUTLASS wrapper. we should audit the macro usages; might be hiding assumptions.
cheng: noted. i'll grep and add unit test to ensure kernel selection isn't coupled to prefetch compile-time assumption.
perf-bot: update: perf-run 2340 (after rollback) p99=112ms (delta vs baseline +14ms). still marginally higher but within tolerance.
maya: cool — keep monitoring. thanks all. :pray: 
ops: flagged follow-up ticket: INF-5423 (kernel-selector telemetry + calibration re-run).
liam: if anyone wants to reproduce quickly, use the bench matrix script in //tools/bench/experiments/fp8_kv_bounce.sh
maya: ack. ping me if you capture nvprof traces, i'll coordinate nsight sessions.
cheng: filing PR for selector-logs now.
sylvia: will push recalibrated profiles in ~30m.
ops: closing loop once we have canary p99 <120ms for 1h. :clock1:
